chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If you remember while you are in your prayer that you have left out something obligatory from your ablution, then turn back (end your prayer), complete what you forgot from your ablution, and repeat your prayer. And it suffices you for wiping your head if you take the moisture from your beard when you forgot to wipe your head, and you wipe the front of your head with it.
ai.seo_question: What should one do if they realize they missed a part of wudu while praying?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that forgetting an obligatory component of wudu invalidates the prayer, requiring a full restart after completion of the missing act. Notably, the ruling for neglecting head wiping (masah) is lenient: the residual moisture on the beard from washing the face suffices for the head, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the limbs are connected in ablution. This highlights the distinction between forgetting a pillar (rukn) versus a recommended act, emphasizing the integrity of the ritual state during worship.
